subject: error in specifying a latent mediation model?

messages.author: 373e56ec89625c50
messages.subject: error in specifying a latent mediation model?
parts:
lavaan is giving me an error when i'm trying to practice how to specify latent mediation models. i'm using syntax right from the website so i'm not sure what i'm doing wrong. for reference, i'm using lavaan 0.5-14
 
here's what i'm doing:
 

pop.model <-
     
    '#model
     X=~ 0.8*x1 + 0.8*x2 + 0.8*x3 + 0.8*x4
     M=~ 0.8*m1 + 0.8*m2 + 0.8*m3 + 0.8*m4
     Y=~ 0.8*y1 + 0.8*y2 + 0.8*y3 + 0.8*y4 
    
     #variances
     X~~1*X
     M~~1*M
     Y~~1*Y
    
     #covariances
     X ~~ 0.6*M
     Y ~~ 0.6*X
     Y ~~ 0.6*M     
 '
datum <- simulateData(pop.model, sample.nobs=1000)

mod1 <-
     '#model
     X=~ NA*x1 + x2 + x3 + x4
     M=~ NA*m1 + m2 + m3 + m4
     Y=~ NA*y1 + y2 + y3 + y4 
    
     #variances
     X~~1*X
     M~~1*M
     Y~~1*Y
    
     #covariances
     X ~~ M
     Y ~~ X
     Y ~~ M
        
     #latent regressions
      M ~ X
      Y ~ X + M      
 '
fit <- sem(mod1, data=datum

 

the moment i try to run the sem() function on fit, i get this error:
 
 fit <- sem(mod1, data=datum)
Error in lavParseModelString(model) :
  lavaan ERROR: duplicate model element in: M~X

i have tried similar syntax in path analysis and have never got any probelms. and the general set-up for 'mod1' is basically a copy-paste from the "Software for Mediation Analysis" presentation, slide #21
 
what am i doing wrong?

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: error in specifying a latent mediation model?
parts:
You have both regression dependencies and covariances in the model.  Given the regression paths, the covariance statements tell lavaan that you want to covary predictors with the residuals from the same regressions .  Such a model will not be identified (without instrumental variables).  The lavaan error message says, "Surely that is a syntax error."
--Ed Rigdon

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: error in specifying a latent mediation model?
parts:
You have the same problem, since Y is dependent on M.  Correlation of this disturbance with the predictor M is a violation of a major least squares regression assumption.  Moreover, think of the covariance matrix of X, M, Y.  It has 6 unique elements.  Your unknowns are #1 variance of X, # 2- #3 residual variances of M and Y, #4 #5 #6 the three regression paths.  That's all you can estimate.
--Ed Rigdon
